mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT remains deeply depressed while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, discretionary shopping trips stay suppressed and RETAIL_REC declines further over the next four weeks because fewer commuters generate fewer same-day retail visits.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-28-day mean over the next 28 days despite TRANSIT staying below -35 and RESIDENTIAL staying above +5 for most weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A further week-on-week fall in WORKPLACES below the recent range signals weaker weekday movement and less spillover spending, which pushes RETAIL_REC down within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below -17 after being above that level in the prior week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within the next 14 days after WORKPLACES crosses below -17 from a higher value.

mechanism_narrative: A synchronized deterioration across TRANSIT and WORKPLACES indicates renewed movement restraint, and that regime reduces retail footfall over the next four weeks as nonessential trips are postponed.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stays below -40 and WORKPLACES stays below -15 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is flat or higher over the next 28 days even though both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain below the stated thresholds for two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS mobility rebounds strongly from a negative shock, leisure demand shifts back toward outdoor recreation and away from malls and high streets, reducing RETAIL_REC over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 8 points week-on-week after a prior week below -20
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall in the week after PARKS jumps by 8 or more points from a week below -20.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GROCERY_PHARM alongside elevated RESIDENTIAL implies more at-home consumption and fewer impulse retail trips, so RETAIL_REC weakens over four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days while GROCERY_PHARM stays above -5 and RESIDENTIAL stays above +8.

mechanism_narrative: A short-run improvement in TRANSIT indicates more regular trip chaining and higher weekday circulation, which raises RETAIL_REC within two weeks as more trips combine with shopping stops.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by at least 3 points from one week to the next while staying below -35
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within 14 days after TRANSIT improves by 3 or more points from a still-depressed level.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both recover together, the city is exiting movement suppression and retail spending follows the same path, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -15 and TRANSIT rises above -40 in the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its last-28-day mean over the next 28 days despite both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT crossing their thresholds upward together.

mechanism_narrative: In a steady but cautious mobility regime, a higher RESIDENTIAL share means people are spending more time near home and making fewer discretionary shopping excursions, so RETAIL_REC drifts down within four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days while RESIDENTIAL remains above +8 throughout most of the horizon.
